snapshot.title: TNPSC Geography: Physical Features of Tamil Nadu
snapshot.exam_hook: 🎯 TNPSC Geography Hook: Doddabetta: Highest (2,637m). Coast: 1076km. Shervaroy: Salem. Kolli: Namakkal. Gaps connect to Kerala. Coromandel coast.

quick_notes.title: Location & Boundaries
quick_notes.detail: Latitude: 8°4' N to 13°35' N. Longitude : 76°18' E to 80°20' E. Boundaries : Kerala (W), Karnataka (NW), Andhra (N), Bay of Bengal (E), Indian Ocean (S). Coastal length : ~1076 km (2nd longest after Gujarat).
quick_notes.explanation: The state of Tamil Nadu is located in southern India. Its position on the Earth is measured by latitude, which is the distance north or south of the equator, ranging from 8 degrees 4 minutes north to 13 degrees 35 minutes north, and by longitude, the distance east or west of the prime meridian, ranging from 76 degrees 18 minutes east to 80 degrees 20 minutes east. Tamil Nadu shares land borders with Kerala to the west, Karnataka to the northwest, and Andhra Pradesh to the north, while its eastern coast is bounded by the Bay of Bengal and its southern tip touches the Indian Ocean. The coastline of Tamil Nadu, meaning the length of its border along the sea, is approximately 1076 kilometers, which is the second longest coastline among all Indian states, after Gujarat.

quick_notes.title: Western Ghats in TN
quick_notes.detail: Starts from Nilgiris to Kanyakumari. Major Hills : Nilgiris, Anaimalai, Palani Hills, Cardamom Hills, Varushanadu, Pothigai Hills. Highest Peak : Doddabetta (2, 637m) in Nilgiris. Anaimudi is in Kerala but near the border.
quick_notes.explanation: The Western Ghats are a long mountain range that runs along the western side of India, and in the state of Tamil Nadu (TN), they start from the Nilgiris district in the north and continue all the way down to Kanyakumari district at the southern tip. The major hills in this part of the range include the Nilgiris, Anaimalai, Palani Hills, Cardamom Hills, Varushanadu, and Pothigai Hills. The highest peak in the Tamil Nadu section of the Western Ghats is Doddabetta, which stands 2,637 meters tall and is located in the Nilgiris. Another famous peak, Anaimudi, is actually in the neighboring state of Kerala, but it is very close to the Tamil Nadu border.

quick_notes.title: Eastern Ghats in TN
quick_notes.detail: Discontinuous range. Major Hills : Javadi, Shevaroy (Salem), Kalrayan, Pachaimalai (Trichy), Kolli Hills (Namakkal). Highest peak : Shervaroyan Temple (1, 623m).
quick_notes.explanation: The Eastern Ghats are a mountain range that runs along the eastern coast of India, but in Tamil Nadu (TN), this range is not a continuous line of mountains; instead, it appears as separate, broken groups of hills. The major hills in Tamil Nadu that are part of the Eastern Ghats include the Javadi Hills, the Shevaroy Hills (located near Salem), the Kalrayan Hills, the Pachaimalai Hills (near Trichy, also spelled Tiruchirappalli), and the Kolli Hills (in Namakkal district). The highest peak in this entire Tamil Nadu section of the Eastern Ghats is called Shervaroyan Temple, which stands 1,623 meters (about 5,325 feet) above sea level. A peak is simply the very top point of a mountain or hill, and a meter is a unit of length equal to roughly 3.28 feet.

quick_notes.title: Passes (Gaps)
quick_notes.detail: Palakkad Gap (between Nilgiris and Anaimalai), Shencottah Gap, Aralvaimozhi Gap, Achankovil Gap. These gaps are crucial for trade and monsoon winds.
quick_notes.explanation: TITLE: Passes (Gaps) A "gap" is a natural low point or opening in a mountain range that allows people, goods, and wind to pass through. The Palakkad Gap is a major break in the Western Ghats mountains located between the Nilgiri Hills and the Anaimalai Hills, and it is the most important gap for trade and for the southwest monsoon winds to enter Tamil Nadu. The Shencottah Gap is another opening in the Western Ghats that connects the state of Kerala to the Tirunelveli region of Tamil Nadu. The Aralvaimozhi Gap is a narrow pass near the southern tip of the Western Ghats, historically used for trade and travel between Tamil Nadu and Kerala. The Achankovil Gap is a pass in the southern Western Ghats that also provides a route for movement and wind. All these gaps are crucial because they allow monsoon winds to bring rain to the inland areas and serve as historic trade routes connecting the coastal regions with the interior.

quick_notes.title: Coastal Plains
quick_notes.detail: Known as the Coromandel Coast (Cholamandalam). Features : Marina Beach (2nd longest in world), Gulf of Mannar (Biosphere Reserve), Palk Strait.
quick_notes.explanation: Coastal plains are flat, low-lying areas of land next to the sea. The coastal plains along the eastern coast of southern India are called the Coromandel Coast, also known as Cholamandalam, which means the kingdom of the Chola dynasty. A famous part of the Coromandel Coast is Marina Beach, which is the second longest urban beach in the world, stretching about 13 kilometers. Another feature is the Gulf of Mannar, which is a large bay of the Indian Ocean located between India and Sri Lanka, and it is also a Biosphere Reserve, meaning it is a protected area that helps conserve the rich marine life and habitats there. Finally, the Palk Strait is a narrow strip of sea that separates southern India from the island of Sri Lanka, connecting the Bay of Bengal to the Gulf of Mann

For TNPSC, knowing the highest peaks (Doddabetta) and the various mountain passes like Palakkad and Shencottah is vital. Let's map your home state today.
